item.title: When the Doctor Becomes the Patient
item.description: As doctors, we are trained to be warriors of science — armed with stethoscopes, clinical precision, and the unshakable calm that’s expected of us. We learn to silence our fears, suppress our emotions, and steel ourselves against the pain of others. We are taught how to heal. But nothing — no textbook, no lecture, no residency rotation — prepares us for the day we are the ones lying in the hospital bed. The day the healer becomes the wounded. The doctor becomes the patient.

item.title: A journey through wisdom, insights, and preparation tales.
item.description:
My Preparation Materials

Preparing for NEET PG isn’t just about hard work — it’s about being smart with your resources. I try to carefully manage which materials I use for each subject, depending on what fits best. Personally, I prefer Marrow videos and notes as my core resources, but I also make sure to explore other valuable content from BTR and various free online tutorials and courses.

To crack NEET PG, you have to be focused, passionate, and wise in your preparation choices. It’s not just about what you study, but how you approach it.

item.title: A Day in the Life of a Medical Student: My First Surgery Rotation
item.description:
The Morning Hustle

The day began at 6:00 AM. I packed my bag with my trusty stethoscope, surgical cap, and a notebook to jot down everything I learned. By 7:00 AM, I was in the hospital, scrubbing in for the morning ward rounds. The surgery department was buzzing with activity—nurses preparing instruments, residents reviewing patient charts, and consultants discussing the day’s cases.

During the rounds, I observed how the team meticulously reviewed each patient’s progress. From post-operative care to managing complications, every detail mattered. I was struck by how the surgeons balanced clinical expertise with empathy, reassuring patients and their families with a calm demeanor.
